chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: Artwork and markings on band arrangements
summary: Barnet describes sidemen drawing, sometimes pornographic, on parts, and copyist Emil Charlap's coloured cartoons.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You ought to see some of the art work I've got on some of my old arrangements, the guys who have got nothing else to do but draw.
You mean there's a lot of guys with --
Oh, there was an amazing amount of them, that they would sit back there and draw all kinds of -- some of them very pornographic, but nevertheless, it was art work.

I know when Kirstin Howell called John from my house, John told her to tell whoever it was that played lead trumpet in "Chorus Line" in Los Angeles, that he sure did appreciate the art work that arrived in Chicago, because the first trumpet music for "Chorus Line" was completely covered with pornographic drawings.

You know, the way some of those arrangements were marked up, every guy that would get in the band would have his own way of marking what was going on, and it's remarkable sometimes that a guy could even find out what he was supposed to do, I mean if you called a substitute in for some reason. They must have sat down and cried, because maybe this has been through a half a dozen different trumpet players, and they've all marked it differently. The same thing, but they've got a different way of marking it. It's -- I've got some old arrangements home there -- we had a copyist by the name of Emil Charlap, and he was a real artist, and he would draw these things in color on all the parts, actual pictures. Very humorous always.
